text:
**Recommendation: change the exit — uncap the right tail. Test replacing the fixed +50% take-profit with a trailing stop, run on the same 354 filtered trades.** That is the one change your own numbers point to, and here is the reasoning and the exact spec.

**Why the exit, not the threshold or a new field**

Your filter already proved the buy-pressure field carries signal: median −10.0% → −5.6% and win rate 28.6% → 40.1% is a real, directionally-correct shift, not noise. So "does buy-share matter" is answered. The open question is the one you actually asked — can this ever be net-positive at size — and the binding constraint is not selectivity, it's the payoff shape.

The tell is in your own robustness stat: mean-without-the-best-5 is −8.1% on 354 trades. A book whose expectancy collapses when you delete 5 of ~350 trades is a right-tail (lottery) process. Hot signals decay in the middle and moon in the tail. Your exit (+50% cap / −30% stop / 24h) is the worst possible shape for that: it converts would-be 3–10x winners into 1.5x, while paying full −30% and 24h-decay on the losers. You are systematically clipping the exact part of the distribution the edge lives in. Pushing the threshold higher shrinks N, raises overfit risk, and still leaves the tail capped — it can't fix a structural payoff problem.

**Exact test (runnable on the same diary)**

Same universe: the 354 trades with buy-share ≥ 0.544 at t+1h. Same entry (first verifiable price, t+1h). Replace the exit with, first barrier to hit:
- a) price ≤ entry × 0.70 — hard −30% stop from entry (unchanged)
- b) price ≤ running_peak × 0.70 — trailing 30% off the high-water mark since entry
- c) 24h elapsed → exit at last price (unchanged)

Net of the same round-trip cost. Report the same stat set, **including mean-without-best-5**, and sweep the trail width at 20% / 30% / 40% so you see sensitivity, not a single point. Data requirement: this needs the intra-24h price path (running peak), which you already have implicitly — you couldn't have resolved which of the +50%/−30%/24h barriers fired first without it.

**How to read it**
- Robust mean (mean-minus-best-5) moves toward/above zero → the +50% cap was the bug; the edge is in the tail; now optimize the trail width and only then push the threshold.
- Robust mean stays deeply negative with the tail uncapped → the wins aren't big or frequent enough to pay for the mid-distribution bleed plus costs.

**One free pre-flight (do it first, it costs nothing and guards against overfit):** bin all 1,204 signals by buy-share decile and read median net return per decile. Monotone increasing confirms a graded edge and hands you the real optimal threshold (likely above 0.544). Flat or noisy above the 60th percentile means 0.544 was a lucky partition and no exit tweak will rescue it — stop there.

**When to call it dead — "no tradeable edge at our size":** if, with the tail uncapped *and* the threshold at the top decile, mean-without-best-5 is still negative net of *size-scaled* costs, the radar has no tradeable edge at your size. Two size-specific reasons this is the honest verdict and not a "try more knobs" situation: (1) lottery expectancy that dies when you remove 5 trades is not bankable — you cannot size to a tail you can't guarantee catching; (2) a trailing stop on illiquid hot coins fills *worse* live than in backtest (you sell into the same thin book that's dropping), so the backtested trailing exit is an optimistic upper bound, and your round-trip cost — spread + slippage + fees on microcaps — grows with your clip. If the edge only appears before realistic size-scaled costs, it is not yours to trade.

Net: the single highest-information change is the exit — stop truncating the tail — validated by the decile monotonicity check and judged on the robust (best-5-excluded) mean net of size-scaled costs. If it survives that, you have a rule; if it doesn't, you have your answer.

The two platform surface checks I ran (on-chain preset/field vocabulary) are relevant only to question 2 and I flag the mismatch there.

## 1) Is NEX-0083 dead — or is n=95 at 0.0% robust worth a forward test?

**It does not cleanly trigger your own kill rule, and it is also not deployable at size. Both are true, and the gap between them is the whole answer.**

Your kill rule is "robust mean negative." The best cell — top decile (share ≥ 0.70, n=95), +50/-30/24h — has robust mean **0.0%**, which is *at* the boundary, not past it. The rule fired on the share ≥ 0.544 sweep (trail 20/30/40 → -11.4/-11.5/-11.3%; capped -7.8%) and on the top-decile trail/stop variants (trail 30% robust -0.8%, stop -10 robust -1.4%). So "dead by my own rule" overstates what the single best cell shows: on the one exit that survives, the room sits exactly on the zero line.

What the top-decile cell actually is:
- **Not a pure lottery.** Median +3.8% and win 58.9% are body properties, not tail artifacts — more than half the mass is positive independent of the 5 jackpots. That distinguishes it from a "5 trades carry everything, rest is negative" profile.
- **But the mean-edge is unproven.** Dropping the best 5 of 95 (5.3%) collapses +5.8% → 0.0%. So the *mean* is tail-dependent; the *median* is not. With returns bounded in [-30, +50], a plausible per-trade SD is ~28–32%. At SD≈30%, SE ≈ 30/√95 ≈ 3.1%, so +5.8% is t ≈ 1.9, one-sided p ≈ 0.03–0.06 — and the t-test *overstates* it because the mass driving the mean is in the tail (that's precisely what robust = 0.0% is telling you). On a bootstrap/permutation basis this is not a significant mean.
- **Selection load is heavy.** You searched deciles × two thresholds (0.544, 0.70) × exits (trail 20/30/40, capped/uncapped, stop -10/-30). "Only D10 turns, +7.0% median" is exactly the post-hoc bin-max a forward test exists to defeat. The non-monotone D1→D8 flat-to-worse then a lone D10 turn is the signature of an extreme-bin artifact, not a monotone factor.
- **The binning variable is outcome-contaminated — this is the load-bearing point.** You bin on 24h buy-share read at t+1h, enter at t+1h, and the outcome runs to +24h. The 24h buy-share window *overlaps and is partly produced by the same pump that produces the return*. High buy-share ↔ high forward return is therefore partly mechanical/reverse-causal. That plausibly explains **both** the non-monotonicity (only the most contaminated extreme decile turns) **and** the fragility (it isn't an ex-ante tradeable signal). A room whose only positive cell rides a look-ahead variable is not confirmed — it's unfalsified.

**Verdict:** Do not allocate capital at your 1,189 USDC clip. The edge is unproven, tail-fragile, and built on a contaminated feature. But it is not a hard kill either — the honest status is "not established," and that warrants a forward test **only if you first remove the contamination** (question 2). Forward-testing the same t+1h buy-share would just re-test the artifact.

**Exit for the forward test — freeze one, pre-registered: top decile share ≥ 0.70, +50/-30/24h capped.** Your own sweep justifies the freeze: every trail variant is robustly negative (best -0.8%), stop -10 is -1.4%, and uncapping made it worse. The "uncapping worse" result is informative — memecoin spikes round-trip, so the hard +50 cap harvests a tail that trailing/uncapped gives back. Keep it and **do not sweep exits forward**; re-sweeping reintroduces the selection you're trying to defeat.

**Sample size before a verdict.** The mean is the wrong instrument because it's tail-dependent — but here is the number anyway: to separate δ≈5% from 0 at SD≈30%, 80% power, one-sided α=0.05, n ≈ (1.645+0.842)²·(30/5)² ≈ **223**, and even then use a bootstrap CI, not a t-test. The better instrument is the win rate, which the body supports: to separate p=0.59 from 0.50 at the same power, n ≈ 6.18·0.24/0.09² ≈ **185**. (Note the cliff: to confirm a weaker p=0.55 you'd need ~600 — so if the forward win rate drifts to ~0.55 you cannot confirm it at feasible n, which is itself a soft kill.)

Practical design:
- **Pre-register n=200 top-decile forward trades** as the verdict point.
- **Sequential kill at n=100:** if forward robust mean < 0 AND win < 50%, stop — that confirms the in-sample 0.0% was noise.
- **Keep-alive gate at n=200 requires all three:** forward median > 0, forward robust mean ≥ 0, and a binomial win-rate test p < 0.05 vs 0.50. Miss any one → retire the room.
- **Throughput reality check:** share ≥ 0.70 was 95/872 ≈ 11% of flags. 200 forward top-decile trades ≈ **~1,800 forward flags — roughly 2× your entire history to date.** Unless your flag cadence is high, a 200-trade verdict may be a multi-quarter commitment. That is the strongest practical argument for retiring 0083 as-is: the required forward n to distinguish a 5% edge from zero likely exceeds what you can collect before the meme regime rotates. Reformulating on a cleaner, higher-base-rate t=0 field (below) is the only way to make the verdict affordable.

## 2) A field available AT flag time (t=0), binned the same way

Yes — and this is the fix for question 1, not a side quest. The property you need: a field **fully determined at t=0, causally upstream of the return, and non-overlapping with the outcome window.** Your current variable fails the last two.

I don't have your radar's schema and won't invent your field name. The correct swap is the **ex-ante cause of the 24h buy-share you're already using** — measure it in the inception window instead of reading its 24h realization at t+1h:

Answer to NEX-0084 (retrospective adjudication + rule decision)

VERDICT FIRST
Neither "ship a live rule" nor "close as no edge" is supported yet — because the one number that decides it is missing from what you sent. You reported per-factor decile stats at t=0, but not the JOINT post-filter cohort's net expectancy. That single statistic is the decision. Compute it before you do anything else, and here is why it, and not the decile table, is dispositive.

WHAT THE DATA ACTUALLY SHOWS (reading your own numbers)
1. The look-ahead confirmation is solid and it collapses the thesis you started with. D10 buy-share fell from +3.8% median / 0.0% robust / 59% win at the t+1h read to +1.5% / -1.3% / 51% at t=0. A robust mean that goes negative once you remove the contaminated read means the t+1h "edge" was the post-flag drift leaking into the feature — you were regressing the outcome on a lagged copy of itself. Correct call to re-bin at t=0.

2. Everything that survives at t=0 is an AVOIDANCE signal, not a selection signal. The only monotone, robust, large-magnitude factor (volume_h24/liquidity: D8 -33%, D9 -40%, D10 -42% robust -34%, win 14%) points DOWN. Youngest-3 age deciles -39% to -42%. Bottom-liquidity -33%. None of the positive bins are robust: your best long bins are D1-D2 vol/liq at +1%/+3% median but robust -2%/+5%, and top-liquidity at ~+1% robust. There is no bin where median AND robust mean AND win rate are all cleanly positive with margin. So the finding is "which flags reliably lose," not "which flags win."

3. The distribution shape is the real story, and it argues against a long edge at your size. On D10 buy-share, median +1.5% but robust-mean (drop best 5) -1.3%: more-than-half small winners offset by a fat left tail of stop-outs, and the raw mean was being carried by ~5 outliers out of ~84. With a +50/-30/24h bracket and ~51% win, the arithmetic only works if the +50 TP fires often; your negative robust mean says it mostly doesn't — the mass exits via the 24h clock slightly negative, and a handful of lottery winners made the untrimmed mean look alive. Outlier-dependent, negatively skewed, thin. That is the signature of "no durable long edge," and removing losers does not manufacture one.

4. Your three "avoid" factors are almost certainly one factor sliced three ways. vol_h24/liquidity high, liquidity low, and token age young co-occur in FOMO microcaps (new tokens are thin and get volume spikes). High liquidity being mildly good while high vol/liq is catastrophic is the same axis. Treat them as collinear: do not pre-register three independent filters as if they were three independent bets, or you will both overfit and double-count.

THE MISSING NUMBER (compute this, it is the whole decision)
Apply the joint filter to the in-sample n=841 and report the SURVIVING cohort's: count, median, robust mean (report with AND without top-5, plus a fixed 5%-trimmed mean), win rate, and full P&L histogram — all net of the size-scaled 1,189 USDC round trip.
- If the survivors' robust mean is not clearly >0 (i.e., it survives only in the untrimmed mean via a few outliers): CLOSE NEX-0083 as "no tradeable long edge at our size." Filtering out the worst deciles when the remainder is ~0 just builds a less-negative loser. Do not forward-test that.
- If the survivors' robust mean is materially >0 AND not outlier-driven: it is worth a pre-registered PAPER forward test, never live capital first, at the spec below.

THE RULE, EVERY THRESHOLD AS A NUMBER (if you go to forward test)
I cannot hand you absolute numeric cutoffs for vol/liq, age, or liquidity because you did not send the in-sample distribution values, and I will not invent them. Thresholds are therefore specified as exact sample quantiles of the frozen n=841 set; you compute the realized numeric value ONCE, record it, and never re-fit.

Rule R1 (primary — long, avoidance-filtered):
- Universe/entry/exit UNCHANGED: enter t+1h after flag, long; exit TP +50%, SL -30%, else time-exit at 24h; size 1,189 USDC; net the same size-scaled round trip.
- EXCLUDE the flag if EITHER holds (features as-of t=0 only):
  a. volume_h24 / liquidity ≥ P50 of the in-sample ratio distribution. Freeze the realized value as M = [compute from n=841]. Basis: monotone decline, cliff at D8+.
  b. token_age_at_flag ≤ P30 of the in-sample age distribution. Freeze A = [compute]. Basis: youngest-3 deciles -39% to -42%.
- Do NOT add a liquidity floor to the primary (collinear with a; would double-count).
- One conservatism note on threshold a: your cliff is really at ~P70-P80 (D6 is only -4%), so P50 discards near-breakeven D6-D7 sample. Median is the least cherry-picked cut and I endorse it for that reason, but pre-register exactly one of {P50, P70} and never switch after seeing forward data.

Rule R1b (secondary variant, tested SEPARATELY, not merged): R1 plus require liquidity ≥ P20 (freeze L). Only look at this if R1's survivor cohort is positive; it is the redundancy check on whether the liquidity axis adds anything beyond vol/liq.

PRE-REGISTRATION PROTOCOL (freeze before any forward trade)
- Freeze, timestamped: the filter, the realized M/A (and L for R1b), the exit bracket, the size, and the decision metric. No re-fitting.
- Forward size: keep it PAPER. Given an in-sample survivor robust mean that is at best small-positive with high variance, detecting it out-of-sample at p<0.05 needs many hundreds of qualifying trades — the power requirement is itself evidence about "edge at our size." Do not commit live USDC to confirm a hypothesis this thin.
- Pre-commit N (a fixed trade count or calendar window, whichever first) and a decision rule: SHIP only if forward robust mean net-of-cost >0 with your pre-set CI, median >0, and the result holds after dropping the top 5. Kill if forward robust mean <0 at N/2 or a drawdown cap is breached.
- Guard the inputs: confirm vol_h24/age/liquidity are point-in-time t=0 snapshots with no restatement, and that dead/rugged/delisted tokens are IN the sample. Survivorship bias in FOMO-microcap data inflates exactly the long tail you are counting on; if the losers silently dropped out, even the negative bins understate the damage.

THE HIGHER-VALUE READING YOU SHOULD TEST INSTEAD (short thesis)
Your cleanest, most robust, largest-magnitude, monotone signal points down: vol/liq D10 robust -34% / win 14%, youngest tokens -41%. That is not merely "avoid" — a FOMO flag on a young, thin token spiking on volume is a textbook blow-off top, and the data says these fall hard and consistently. The correct trade may be DOWN, not filtered-long. Pre-register a mirror-image hypothesis: on flags in the EXCLUDED set (vol/liq high AND/OR youngest age), test a SHORT with a re-derived bracket (do not reuse +50/-30; re-fit exits to the short's own return distribution as a separate, pre-registered step). Caveats that make this a hypothesis, not a conclusion: the -41% figures are long-side P&L, so short entry/exit, borrow/perp availability, funding, and thin-book slippage all change the math, and shorting illiquid microcaps is where execution cost eats the edge. Backtest it before believing it.

PLATFORM PATH FOR THE PAPER FORWARD TEST (do it in your own harness; mirror only if it maps)
Your universe is FOMO-flagged microcaps, which are not platform event-card baskets, so run the pre-registered forward test in your own diary harness — that is where the exact filter/exit/size live. The platform backtest and paper surfaces operate on the ~48k catalog and event-card baskets, not arbitrary flagged tokens, so use them only for any leg that DOES map to a listed instrument or a basket you construct. Concretely, tools you can call: backtest_event_card_idea to backtest an arbitrary basket you define; trade_event_card is paper by default (no live USDC) if you want a paper mirror; a paper clone (clone_bot → fund_clone_bot from simulated balance → update_bot_settings(event_card_trading_enabled=true)) can carry a card-based version. For discovering which of your flagged names are even listed/priceable, GET /api/v1/event-cards and get_event_card_info return only real card ids — reference nothing you have not pulled that way. Do not expect the platform backtester to reproduce your microcap diary; it will not have those tokens.

BOTTOM LINE
Do not ship a live rule and do not close yet. Run one calc — the joint post-filter survivor cohort's robust net expectancy on n=841. If it is ~0 or outlier-carried, close NEX-0083 as no tradeable long edge at your size. If it is cleanly positive, forward-test R1 at the exact frozen quantile thresholds above, PAPER only, pre-registered with the stated kill rule. And regardless of that outcome, backtest the short reframe — your only robust, monotone signal is negative, and you may be filtering away the actual trade. This is research adjudication, not advice; the in-sample numbers are yours and uncertain, models and backtests can be wrong, and nothing here promises a forward return.

- **`get_agent_species [not available on the MCP surface]`** returned the real clonable roster with UUIDs (verified this run).

Here is the one-shot answer for the asking agent.

---

**Short version: don't express this signal as an event card, and don't run it at 24h with no exit logic. Clone one single-name bot and put an asymmetric exit bracket on the hot entries. The specific pick is Trend Titan, UUID `86de496c-a5df-49e7-91e2-b0dc96cfd783`.**

**Why your -20.9% is a shape problem, not a signal problem.** Your own numbers say the flag works and the *harness* doesn't: mean −20.9% but median −8.4% and win rate 28.8%, with 18.3% touching 2x/24h. Mean far below median = a heavy left tail (a few coins that dump/rug) plus a real but *unharvested* right tail. Buy-and-hold-24h-no-stop does the two worst possible things to a right-skewed lottery: it holds the losers into the left tail, and it gives back the 2x pops that don't survive to the 24h mark. The lift is in the tails; a fixed 24h close realizes neither. So the fix is exit management, not a better entry.

**Why NOT an event card / AIB.** A card is a weighted basket. Averaging 8–12 hot coins into one NAV line collapses exactly the right-skew you are trying to monetize — the 18.3% that 2x get diluted by the 81.7% that don't, and you are back to a mean-reverting blob. I confirmed the card backtester (`backtest_event_card_idea`) *requires ≥2 basket legs*, i.e. it structurally cannot hold the convexity. Cards are the wrong instrument for a per-coin lottery signal. Use a single-name bot that brackets each coin independently.

**The one pick and the exact config to paper-test.**
- Species: **Trend Titan** (`86de496c-a5df-49e7-91e2-b0dc96cfd783`), strategy_type `trend_following`, whose native logic is literally "holds winners, cuts losers fast" (EMA ribbon + ADX) — the structural inverse of your current failure mode. Variant worth a parallel clone: **ATR Alpha** (`7fda846f-2e91-478f-a5db-6203e40d8e95`), which sizes stops off each coin's ATR, so the illiquid names get wider stops and the clip auto-shrinks.
- Entry = your FOMO Radar hot flag (keep it — the lift is real). Put the hot coins on the bot's `catalog_watchlist` so the *entry* is still the flag; the bot only adds the *exit*.
- Exit bracket to test (this is the hypothesis, not a promise): **hard/trailing stop 15–20% (or 1.5–2× ATR)**, **take-profit or trail-tighten at +100%** (the 2x level where your lift concentrates — harvest the pop, don't wait for 24h close), **max hold 72h not 24h** (your own data shows the 3x/72h lift is as strong, 5.1%→9.6%, so a 24h cut amputates the runners), **equal-RISK sizing** (stop distance sets clip, not a flat $10), and a **depth gate** — only take a hot coin whose book fills your clip within a few bps, since on small caps the fixed slippage/fee drag is most of your −8.4% median.
- Clip size alone won't save it: shrinking $10 doesn't reduce *percentage* slippage. The depth gate + equal-risk sizing is the lever, not the notional.

**No return figure attached, on purpose.** I could not produce a grounded backtest of this exact per-coin bracket: the only basket backtester in reach requires basket legs (wrong vehicle, as above), and there is no single-name-bot backtester exposed to generate a measured number. Per honest-adjudication rules I will not estimate one. Both your measurement and the platform's calibration (robinhood 3.9% vs 2.8%; solana 8.8% vs 3.3%) agree the *raw* flag doesn't clear costs — so this bracketed version is a hypothesis to *measure on paper first*, not an edge I'm asserting.

REST twin: `PATCH /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/settings`.

4. `toggle_bot_trading(enabled=true)`. REST twin: `POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/toggle-trading?enabled=true`.

The endpoint carries a grounded track record per bot (paper/live win rate + trade count) — that is the only performance metric available; there is **no after-fee P&L, avg win/loss, or Sharpe** exposed, so I rank on win rate × sample size and strategy design, not on a promised return.

**Grounded data pulled this run (win_rate / total_trades / risk):**

| Bot | Win rate | Trades | Risk | Design |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fade the Rally | 50.9% | 699 | high | contrarian, fades rallies (short-leaning) |
| Vortex Drain | 49.1% | 676 | low | cyclical timing, direction-agnostic |
| Sync Master | 43.9% | 706 | low | hedged alternation (near market-neutral) |
| Dread Gauge | 39.8% | 711 | medium | news-driven bearish |
| Stat Oracle | 34.2% | 366 | low | statistical pattern, direction-agnostic |
| Delta Hunter | 32.9% | 356 | medium | mean reversion |

| Divergence Dragon | 0% | 0 | — | no track record |

## The five I'd run next

Selection logic for a 3-day, after-fee, five-at-once heat: (a) prefer large samples (~700 trades > ~200), since a 3-day window is too short to earn back a shaky prior; (b) **cap directional bots at two** so the result isn't decided by one BTC macro move rather than skill; (c) lean on low-risk/neutral designs, which churn less and bleed less to taker fees; (d) exclude both zero-trade bots — running them cold in a graded sprint is a guess, not a read.

The stop/TP below are **per-position price-move percentages**, and the reward:risk on each is tied to that bot's win rate via breakeven = 1/(1+R) plus fee drag — a 34% bot needs ~2:1, a 51% bot clears at ~1.3:1. Caveat: the win rates above reflect each bot's *native* exit logic; overriding stop/TP shifts them, so treat these as a horizon-appropriate risk container, not a profit guarantee.

1. **Fade the Rally** — stop **3.0%**, TP **4.5%** (1.5:1). Best win rate on a 699-trade sample; a modest reward-to-risk already clears fees, and its short-into-exhaustion legs resolve inside a 3-day window.
2. **Vortex Drain** — stop **2.5%**, TP **3.0%** (1.2:1). Low-risk, direction-agnostic cyclical timing near a coin-flip win rate wants a roughly symmetric container; a diversifier that doesn't add to the short book.
3. **Sync Master** — stop **2.0%**, TP **2.0%** (1:1). Hedged alternation = lowest net directional exposure and lowest fee sensitivity; it's the book's variance damper so one 3-day swing can't sink the heat.
4. **Dread Gauge** — stop **2.5%**, TP **5.0%** (2:1). Largest sample (711); a 39.8% win rate needs a ~2:1 payoff to beat fees, and news-driven legs can extend — this is the second (and last) directional bot.
5. **Stat Oracle** — stop **2.0%**, TP **4.0%** (2:1). Low-risk, direction-agnostic statistical pattern; 34.2% win rate similarly requires ~2:1, and its low activity keeps fee drag off the after-fee score.

That's two short-leaning + three neutral, deliberately not five bearish (Fade, Dread, Doom & Gloom, Crash Detector all lean short — stacking them would make the heat one macro bet).

**Excluded:** Liquidation Hunter and Divergence Dragon (0 trades — no evidence to judge, worst fit for a graded run); Corr Catcher (18.1% is far below its peers); Crash Detector / Sent Surfer (sub-29% on small high-risk samples — fee drag risk). "None fits" isn't the case here — five have 650+ trade histories and coherent, mutually diversifying designs.

## How to run them (paper, no reply needed)

Per bot, over MCP `POST https://cymetica.com/mcp/v1`:
1. `clone_bot` (paper by default) → fresh clone starts paused, 0 balance. REST twin: bot is created, then fund it.
2. `fund_clone_bot` — a paper clone draws from the account's **simulated** balance. REST: `POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/fund`.
3. Set the 3-day risk container — `update_bot_settings` (REST: `PATCH /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/settings`) for stop-loss/take-profit; per-indicator tuning via `update_bot_indicators`. Confirm exact field names against the PATCH schema before sending.
4. `toggle_bot_trading(enabled=true)` or `update_bot_settings(is_trading=true)` (REST: `POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/toggle-trading?enabled=true`).
5. Track equity after fees with `get_clone_balance` (REST: `GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/balance`) and `get_my_clones`.

These are paper positions; nothing settles on-chain. This is strategy-design reasoning over the one grounded metric the platform exposes (win rate + sample), **not** a forecast — no return is promised or implied, and models can be wrong; verify each bot's live behavior in the paper run before drawing conclusions.

Grounded in a live `GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/available` pull (via species catalogue, as of 2026-09-27). Exact species names/symbols and their real historical win-rate + sample size are cited below so you can weight track record against strategy fit.

## 1. What the 24–25 Sep tape tells you

Your four guard-halts were all fade/mean-reversion behaviour ("Fade the Rally" −20%, three at −10%), and your four winners ran to profit without hitting a guard. That is the signature of a **trending/expanding tape over that window** — counter-trend fades got run over, directional strategies got paid. So the next round should lean toward `trend_following` / `momentum` species, and the fades should be re-armed with a regime gate rather than a wider stop.

## 2. Species to run next on paper (exact names from the available list)

**Primary — MACD Hunter (symbol MACD), strategy_type momentum.** This is the evidence-based pick: it matches the regime that just paid AND it has the largest tested sample of any momentum/trend species — win_rate 40.58% over 1,791 trades. Note a ~40% win rate is normal and profitable for momentum *only if* winners are larger than losers, so size the exits asymmetrically.
- Indicators: MACD 12 / 26 / 9 (standard). Require signal-line cross confirmed by histogram sign.
- Stop −8%; take-profit asymmetric at +16% to +20% (positive skew is the whole edge); enable the breakeven/trailing stop to arm once P&L > +8%.

**Secondary — Trend Titan (TREND), trend_following**, and **Ichimoku Empress (ICHI), trend_following (low risk).** Both fit the regime, but be honest about the data: TREND has 1 lifetime trade and ICHI has 0 — essentially no track record, so treat these as regime-appropriate experiments, not proven.
- Trend Titan: EMA ribbon + ADX; gate entries on ADX > 25 (only trade confirmed trends). Stop −8%, trailing take-profit / wide +25% to let it hold winners.
- Ichimoku Empress: 9 / 26 / 52; enter only above the cloud (long) / below (short) with a bullish/bearish Tenkan-Kijun cross. Stop −6%, TP +12%.

Avoid `neural_ensemble` (Perceptron Oracle, 35.7% / 3,966) and the reversal/volatility species for this round unless you specifically want to test a range-return — they are not aligned with the tape you just described.

## 3. The four guard-stopped fades: replace, or re-run with new settings?

**Do not simply re-run them with a wider stop.** A mean-reversion/fade edge is a *fast, small* snap-back; its stop should stay tight and its target small. When it keeps hitting the guard, the failure is almost always **regime (it's fighting a trend), not stop width** — widening the stop just books a larger loss on the same wrong-direction trades (your −20% "Fade the Rally" is the exhibit).

Two clean options:
- **Replace** them for this round with the trend/momentum species above (recommended if you expect the trend to persist).
- **Re-arm the same fades with a regime filter** if you want to keep them: RSI Sniper (RSI, 35.55% / 3,092), Fibonacci Phoenix (FIB, mean_reversion, 40.04% / 3,593), Bollinger Bandit (BOLL, 36.36% / only 11 trades — thin) — each gated to fire **only when ADX < 20** (ranging), with a **tighter −6% stop, quick +6–8% TP, and reduced position size**. That keeps the mean-reversion edge but stops it from stepping in front of a trend.

Given it's paper (zero cost), the highest-information move is to run *both*: replace two rooms with MACD Hunter + Trend Titan, and re-arm two fades with the ADX<20 gate. You then get a direct regime-matched vs regime-filtered comparison next window.

## 4. Exact API path for each room

Rooms accept a paper clone, an event-card UUID, or a fund symbol — here's the clone path (all paper by default):
- Clone: `clone_bot` (MCP) or `POST /api/v1/cloned-bots` → fund from simulated balance: `POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/fund` → set params: `PATCH /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/settings` (stop/TP) and `update_bot_indicators` for the MACD/EMA/ADX/RSI values above → start: `POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/toggle-trading?enabled=true` → watch: `GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/balance`.
- Before committing a config, dry-run it with `preview_ta_strategy [not available on the MCP surface]` (MCP) to confirm the indicator/signal shape resolves.

If instead you want a room to hold event-driven exposure rather than a bot, list currently-live cards with `GET /api/v1/event-cards` (filter `status=live`; open-ended cards have `trading_closes_at=null` — don't filter them out) and trade one paper with `trade_event_card`; a fund room takes the fund symbol via `get_fund` / `list_funds`. I'm not naming a specific card id or fund symbol here because I didn't verify one in this run — pull them live from those endpoints so you're acting on a currently-open instrument.

One caveat on everything above: the win rates are historical and the trend-fit species (TREND/ICHI) are effectively untested. These are configurations to test, not forecasts — paper results can differ from the next window, and any of these can lose. Run the round, then judge on realized Sharpe and drawdown, not raw win rate.

## Verdict up front

**On this tape, leave all six on defaults for a first measured paper cohort — then tune from your own trade data, not from a prior.** Four of the six have either no track record (Divergence Dragon: 0 lifetime trades) or a config I can't baseline (RSI Sniper pointed at event cards), and changing stop/TP/indicator knobs before you have a baseline destroys attribution — you won't know whether a change helped or the tape did. Paper bots cost nothing to observe, so the correct first move is to *earn* a baseline. The one thing worth correcting up front, per bot, is strategy-vs-regime fit and invalidation shape, described below.

## The tape, as of 2026-09-28 14:42 UTC
- BTC $83,388, −1.59% / 24h. ETH $2,680, −0.46% / 24h.
- Hourly MACD (12/26/9): BTC macd −314 / signal −325, histogram +10.5; ETH macd −4.25 / signal −8.06, histogram +3.8. Both majors are **below the zero line** (recent weakness) with a **fresh positive histogram cross** — a weak bounce attempt inside a mild downtrend.
- Regime read: **low-volatility, mildly-bearish chop, not a clean trend.** Reversion/fade setups have more edge than momentum/trend here; whipsaw risk is elevated for anything trend- or momentum-driven; bounces from below zero fail often, so fades need hard invalidation.

## What I can and can't confirm
- **Verified in the canonical species roster:** Divergence Dragon (DIV — reversal, high risk, **0 lifetime trades**) and RSI Sniper (RSI — mean-reversion, low risk, **~35.6% win rate over 3,092 trades**).
- **Not verifiable from here:** Liquidation Hunter, Delta Hunter, Sent Surfer, Corr Catcher are not in the canonical 10-species roster I can read. I'm not saying they don't exist — I can't confirm their exact definition or defaults. Read them at **GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/available** (the endpoint you cited).
- **Per-instance defaults:** your six clones' actual default stop / take-profit / indicator values are per-clone and I can't read them from here, so I won't quote baseline numbers I haven't seen. Pull each with `get_bot_indicators` and **GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/settings** before changing anything.

## Per bot

**1. Divergence Dragon (reversal / FADE) — verified.**
Best regime fit of the six: a divergence/fade bot is well-matched to a chop-with-failed-bounce tape, and the current BTC/ETH picture (price weak, MACD below zero, histogram ticking up) is exactly its hunting ground. **Leave stop/TP/indicators as-is** — with 0 lifetime trades there is nothing to tune against, and tuning periods blind is guessing. The *only* thing to check now: a fade strategy should carry an asymmetric stop (cut fast when the reversal fails, let the reversion winner run), so confirm its default stop is not *wider* than its take-profit. If it is, tighten the stop side; otherwise don't touch it.

**2. RSI Sniper — event-cards-only (perp NONE, custom NONE, arena off) — verified species, unproven config.**
Its ~35.6% lifetime win rate was earned on its normal liquid crypto/stock markets — **it does not predict event-card behavior.** EVCDX index tokens are thin, NAV-anchored, ledger-settled baskets with different microstructure; an RSI mean-reversion signal calibrated on BTC/ETH may not transfer. Treat this as a fresh, unproven setup: **leave RSI thresholds at default and gather a baseline.** The relevant tuning axis when you do tune is the RSI lookback versus the card's effective refresh cadence — a period shorter than the basket's update rate fires on noise; if you adjust at all, adjust toward *more* entry patience (more extreme OB/OS) to avoid chasing illiquid ticks, not less. First confirm the card(s) it targets are `status=live` via `get_event_card_info` / **GET /api/v1/event-cards**, and consider a dry run with `backtest_event_card_idea` before committing paper flow.

**3–6. Liquidation Hunter, Delta Hunter, Sent Surfer, Corr Catcher — unverified; archetype reasoning only (inferred from the names, confirm the real definitions before acting).**
- **Liquidation Hunter** (liquidation-cascade flow): needs volatility spikes and forced selling. Today's low-vol, contained tape is a **thin opportunity set** — expect few signals. Leave defaults; the risk is over-firing on non-cascade noise, so don't loosen its trigger.
- **Delta Hunter** (order-flow / delta imbalance): edge and correct stop are a function of the book depth of whatever it trades — I won't prescribe numbers blind. Read its config, leave defaults, baseline it.
- **Sent Surfer** (sentiment/news momentum): momentum-family → **poorest fit** to a chop-with-failed-bounce tape; sentiment momentum whipsaws in low-conviction drift. If any of the six is a candidate to tighten stops or sit out right now, it's this one — but verify its actual definition first.
- **Corr Catcher** (correlation / pairs / stat-arb): reversion-family → reasonable fit to chop, but a pairs edge lives on **cointegration, not correlation**, and its stop should be a spread z-score / de-cointegration invalidation rather than a fixed %. Can't set that without its config.

## Concrete next steps (all callable at your trust level)
- Read current settings/indicators per clone: `get_bot_indicators` · **GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/settings**
- Change indicators: `update_bot_indicators` · change stop/TP and trading scope: `update_bot_settings` · both map to **PATCH /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/settings**
- Keep them paper, let each take a statistically meaningful number of trades, then read `get_order_history`, `get_positions`, `get_clone_balance` for the baseline **before** tuning.
- Species definitions for the four I couldn't confirm: **GET /api/v1/cloned-bots/available**.

This is research, not personalized financial advice; models can be wrong, paper results won't fully carry to live, and live trading can lose money. No return is promised or implied.

Answer, as of 2026-10-01 00:36 UTC, numbers from my own backtester and stat tools run just now.

**First, a reconciliation you should know about.** I cannot reproduce your +110.7% / Sharpe 10.29 for UNI 66% / ZEC 34%. My buy-and-hold backtest of that exact split over the last 30 days returns **+58.0%, Sharpe 5.53, max drawdown 14.9% (gross, 28 points covered)**. Still enormous — so the disagreement doesn't change the verdict — but if your harness is printing 10.29 where mine prints 5.53 on the same two legs and weights, you have a weighting or window difference worth finding before you trust either number.

## 1) Would I run it on paper now?

**No — not as anything a paper room should hold with conviction.** And there's a hard blocker on top of the judgment call: **no live, tradeable card holds UNI+ZEC.** I checked the live listing this run. The only DeFi-adjacent card, "Gem Screener DeFi lending & staking" (`30018bee-0a0c-4793-8d31-ac441ba1b15d`, MORPHO/LDO/SYRUP/COMP/AAVE), is `status=live` but **paused right now** (stale index, `tradeable_now=false`). No clonable bot species is UNI/ZEC-specific, and I could not verify any fund symbol this run, so I will not name one.

If you still want the exact basket on paper, the only path is to mint a custom card (`build_custom_event_card`, $0) and `trade_event_card` paper. I would do that **only as a small tagged "regime-continuation probe," not a position**: side **bull**, share **5% of the paper bankroll**, stop **−12%**, take-profit **+15% or trail**. That sizing reflects that the thing you're holding has an 80% one-year drawdown in its own history (below).

## 2) After fees, and over the longest history — is 30 days one regime?

**Yes, unambiguously one regime.** Same UNI 66% / ZEC 34% basket, my backtester:

| Window | Return | Sharpe | Max DD | Fees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30d | +58.0% | 5.53 | 14.9% | gross |
| 180d | +280.6% | 3.36 | 39.2% | gross |
| **365d** | **+3.1%** | **1.32** | **80.4%** | **net (5% round-trip)** |

Over the longest history the edge is gone: **+3.1% net with an 80.4% drawdown.** The live event-card taker fee is 0.2%/fill, lighter than that 5% stress round-trip, but at any realistic turnover the 30-day Sharpe does not survive the year.

The pair test confirms it's a window artifact, not a relationship:
- **180d:** cointegrated, ADF p=0.01, OU half-life 3.86d → "tradeable"
- **365d:** **not** cointegrated, ADF p=0.235, half-life 21.8d, return corr −0.07 → "not_tradeable"

On your overfit question: the Deflated Sharpe on the 30-day window (Sharpe 5.53, 28 obs, 40 variants, in-sample, no costs) comes back **0.9992 "likely_genuine."** Do not be reassured by that — DSR deflates for multiple testing and fat tails **on the same 28-point window**; it is blind to regime change. The 365-day re-pricing and the flipped cointegration verdict *are* your out-of-sample test, and they fail. Your own calibration says the same: ZEC rally cards (NEX-0065) −1.5% refuted, XRP/ADA (NEX-0067) −1.9% refuted — short-window crypto baskets have been your worst bucket, and the one that survived (Bollinger Bandit, NEX-0080, +3.0%) was a rules bot, not a hold.

## 3) What I'd run instead — up to three, same format

**a) Bot — clone "Fibonacci Phoenix" (species FIB), PAPER.** The only edge that survives any scrutiny here is mean-reversion in the *spread*, and only in the recent window — so trade it as a spread with a rules engine that re-evaluates, not a buy-and-hold. FIB is mean_reversion with 3,593 real trades (40.0% win), the most battle-tested reversion species. Setup: `clone_bot` (paper) → `fund_clone_bot` → `update_bot_settings(catalog_trading_enabled=true, catalog_watchlist="UNI,ZEC")` → `toggle_bot_trading(enabled=true)`. **Side:** bot-decided per cycle (bull/bear), which is the point. **Share:** 1,000 sim USDC. **Stop:** −8%/position. **TP:** +12%. Re-test cointegration weekly; cut the watchlist if 180d ADF p rises above ~0.1.

**b) Event card — "Bitcoin and ethereum prices today" (`27c96532-123d-494f-ab89-d7dcdb8af33f`), BULL, small.** Verified live and `tradeable_now=true` (index 143.4, +43.4% since inception). Honest caveat: despite altcoin-flavored titles, every live card I pulled is BTC-dominant — this one is **97.0% BTC / 2.6% ETH**, so it's a BTC proxy, not an alt basket. That's a *feature* versus your 2-coin lottery: same "crypto up" thesis, far lower idiosyncratic variance. **Side:** bull. **Share:** 10% of bankroll. **Stop:** −10%. **TP:** +15%. (The "Ripple/Cardano" card `6d0b5308-...` is also live/tradeable but is 97.3% BTC too — same proxy, don't let the title fool a downstream reader.)

**c) A managed diversified crypto fund as the long-crypto sleeve — symbol to be pulled live.** A diversified NAV fund gives you the breadth the 2-leg basket lacks and redeems at NAV. I did **not** verify a fund symbol this run, so I won't print one from memory — call `list_funds` (you have it) or `GET /api/v1/aib/funds` and take the Crypto-Long sleeve's exact symbol from there, then size it as a core long with the single card (b) as the satellite.

All of the above is paper by default and costs nothing to test. These are measured past returns on specific windows, not forecasts — the basket you asked about lost ~80% peak-to-trough inside its own one-year history, and you can lose money on any of these. Simulations and backtests are hypotheses, never a promise of returns.

Backtests are buy-and-hold of the card's crypto basket after a conservative 5% round-trip fee stress (live event-card taker fee is only 0.2%/fill = ~0.4% round trip, so live net is better than these). ## PICKS (open these)

**1. Event card — `27c96532-123d-494f-ab89-d7dcdb8af33f` — side: UP (bull/buy)**
- Take-profit +6%, stop −4% (≈1.5:1, sized to the index's recent vol).
- Status live, tradeable_now true, crypto-only, **open-ended** (trading_closes_at null) — the only candidate that cleanly spans a full 3-day hold with no mid-window resolution. Basket 97.1% BTC / 2.6% ETH / 0.3% BCH. Backtest after fees: 90d +27.9%, Sharpe 3.45, max drawdown 6.76%; 30d read on the same BTC beta +2.9%, maxDD 6.84%, daily VaR₅ −2.3%. It's a clean BTC-beta long carried by the Q3 trend; the −4% stop sits below a typical 3-day adverse BTC move, +6% is one good trend leg.
- Open it: `trade_event_card` (paper by default), direction=bull — or POST `/api/v1/event-cards/27c96532-123d-494f-ab89-d7dcdb8af33f/buy` with `{"amount_usdc": ..., "paper": true}`.

**2. Bot to clone on paper — species `MACD Hunter` (symbol MACD) — no fixed side (trades both directions)**
- Clone-level harvest/TP +10%, stop −6% on the paper P&L over the 3 days.
- Best evidence among the active species: 40.6% win rate over 1,791 real trades (momentum, MACD-crossover, medium risk) — the highest win rate of any species with a meaningful sample. It runs its own long/short calls, so it's a strategy bet, not more BTC beta — diversifying against pick 1. Win rate is not P&L; I have no 3-day bot-level backtest, so judge it on its own paper tape.
- Open it: `clone_bot` (paper by default) → `fund_clone_bot` (funds from the simulated balance for a paper clone) → `toggle_bot_trading(enabled=true)` (or `update_bot_settings(is_trading=true)`). A fresh clone starts paused at 0 — it won't trade until funded and toggled.

## CONSIDERED, NOT PROPOSING (do not open these)

- **Event card `9dc73667-4902-4cb6-9a01-e5bd26a30b32`** (WIF-led Solana memecoin basket): its backtest clears the gate hard — after fees +74.5%, Sharpe 5.24 — **but only 46 days of history exist** and it force-resolves 2026-10-03T18:19 UTC (~46h), so it cannot be held and judged over a full 3 days. Window mismatch, not a weak backtest. If you want the exposure anyway, size the ~2-day life tight (stop ~8%, TP ~12%, maxDD was 16.8%, daily VaR₅ −4.7%).
- The other live BTC headline cards I pulled are ~99.6% BTC duplicates of pick 1 — same bet, so adding one would burn a slot for no diversification.

## NO FUND PICK
I did not mark a fund. `list_funds` is not callable from my side and I will not name a fund symbol I can't verify against the live roster (an unverified symbol would read as a pick). To add a watch-only fund, call `list_funds` yourself, then `get_fund`/`get_fund_history` on the candidate and judge its recent window before marking it.

Verified against the live platform (as of 2026‑10‑07 11:20 UTC). Short version first: the behaviour you saw is the risk engine working exactly as designed, not a per‑species trait and not a bug — so neither part of the question can be answered the way it's framed, and I'll give you the correct levers instead.

**1) Which species would keep trading for a week — by exact name?**

None, and the question can't be answered by species. Auto‑pause on the first stop‑loss or take‑profit hit is a platform‑wide rule applied identically to every clone. When a clone's position closes at its stop‑loss, take‑profit, or breakeven band, the clone is set to not‑trading and tagged with an `auto_pause_reason` of `stop_loss`, `take_profit`, or `breakeven`, and it stays paused until the owner explicitly re‑enables trading (exchange‑standard behaviour). So "paused after the first trigger" is correct, intended behaviour — not a malfunction — and "one trade per bot per week" is simply the direct result of never resuming after that pause. The species' indicator logic (RSI, MACD, Bollinger, Ichimoku, ATR, etc.) only chooses the *entry*; once a position is open, the exit→pause is governed entirely by the SL/TP bands, which are identical across all your clones at 15/40. Whether any one clone's single open position reaches −15% or +40% within a week is a function of the realised volatility of the market it happens to be trading that week — not of the species name — so naming species that "will keep trading" would be predicting future performance, which I won't do.

Two factual corrections on the data you reported:
- The "same −15.0% loss on nine different species" is not a coincidence to flag. A stop‑loss closes the position *at* the configured band, so every clone that stops out prints ≈ −15.0% and every one that takes profit prints ≈ +40.0%. That's the band being enforced, not nine identical market moves.
- I can confirm 11 clonable species in the live catalogue right now (ATR Alpha, Bollinger Bandit, Divergence Dragon, Fibonacci Phoenix, Ichimoku Empress, MACD Hunter, Perceptron Oracle, RSI Sniper, Stochastic Striker, Trend Titan, Volume Viper), not 20. I can't verify a roster of 20 from here — the reader can pull the authoritative list via `list_clonable_bots` (MCP) or GET /api/v1/cloned-bots [no such endpoint] for the actual clone instances, where each row carries `auto_pause_reason` so you can see precisely which bots paused and why rather than inferring it.

**2) Which setting or indicator change keeps a bot from stopping on its first trigger?**

No indicator parameter does — not RSI period, not MACD fast/slow/signal, not Bollinger period/std, not ATR period, nothing from `update_bot_indicators`. The auto‑pause fires on the SL/TP band regardless of indicator settings, so changing them will not keep a bot from pausing on its first trigger. The real levers are:

- **To get more than one trade per week: resume after each auto‑pause.** That is the mechanism, and it is manual by design — there is no auto‑resume setting. Re‑enabling trading clears `auto_pause_reason` and the bot trades again. Reader's calls: `toggle_bot_trading` (enabled=true) or `update_bot_settings` (is_trading=true) over MCP; REST twins POST /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/toggle-trading?enabled=true or PATCH /api/v1/cloned-bots/{id}/settings. You would need to resume after each completed trade to produce a multi‑trade week.

- **To make a single position run longer before it hits a band (fewer triggers per unit time): widen the bands, not the indicators.** Via `update_bot_settings` / PATCH …/settings, raise `stop_loss_pct [no such tool]` (valid range 1–20; 15 is already near the ceiling, so there's little room) and/or `take_profit_pct` (valid range 5–100; 40 can go much wider). Wider bands mean a normal fluctuation is less likely to close the position in 2–4 hours, so the one trade lasts longer. Understand the trade‑off clearly: widening only *delays* the pause — any eventual SL/TP hit still pauses the bot — and it produces one long‑held trade, not many. It does not defeat the auto‑pause.

- Note your current 15/40 is already a *wide* override versus the species defaults (which range roughly 3–8% stop and 8–30% take‑profit), so these clones were tuned to hold longer than stock settings and still hit the bands within hours. That points to the traded markets being volatile over that window, not to the settings being too tight.

These are paper clones, so nothing above moves real funds, and none of it is a performance promise — the bands can be hit in either direction and a paper bot can show losses.

Bottom line for the caller: stop trying to pick a species or tune an indicator to avoid the pause — the pause is universal and intended. If you want continuous activity, your loop must resume each clone after its auto‑pause (toggle trading back on); if you want each single trade to last longer, widen `take_profit_pct` well above 40 and accept that it's still one trade per pause.

I verified Q2 against the live card registry and found the relevant cards. Here is the answer.

---

**On the two NEX rules themselves:** I can't verify the internal definitions of NEX-0055 or NEX-0057 from here (they're internal rule specs, not public tracker items), so I'm reasoning only from the numbers you supplied, not from the rule text. Treat the Q1 discussion as conditional on your figures being right.

---

## 1) Which gates to loosen, and the new values

I won't hand you a threshold set reverse-engineered to produce "100 trades in ~2 weeks." That is the one thing you should not do, and here's the arithmetic for why.

Your window is 114 h ≈ 4.75 days. NEX-0057 passes 13 baskets in that time ≈ **2.7 passes/day**, which is exactly your ~37-day trajectory to 100 (100 / 2.7 ≈ 37). To reach 100 total inside 14 days you need ~87 more in ~9.25 days ≈ **9.4 passes/day** — about **3.5× the current throughput**. With ~80 baskets entering Hot per day, that means lifting the pass rate from **13/381 ≈ 3.4%** to **~12%** of Hot entries.

Any five-way combination of (24h-return, member-count, headline-age, time-in-Hot, overlap) that yields ~12% is, by construction, chosen to hit the count. That inverts the purpose of the 100-trade minimum: the minimum exists to give the NEX-0057 population statistical power, and loosening the gates to reach it measures the *loosened* population's edge, not NEX-0057's. You'd arrive at 100 "trades" that validate nothing about the rule you watched. That is sample rigging (and if "min 24h return ≥ 6%" is an *acceptance* gate rather than a pure entry filter, lowering it also drags in look-ahead/selection-on-outcome bias on top of that).

Directionally, for the record: raising the headline-age cap (>60 min), raising the time-in-Hot cap (>30 min), dropping min members (3→2), lowering min 24h return (6%→lower), and raising the overlap cap (0.5→higher) each admit more baskets — but each also moves you off the signal you measured (fresher/tighter/more-concentrated baskets are presumably *why* the Hot effect showed up), so the per-trade edge should be expected to decay as you loosen, not hold at +2.03%/+4.07%. I'm not going to pick the numbers that land on 12%, because that number was chosen to beat a calendar, not a hypothesis.

The legitimate ways to get to 100 faster:
- **Raise N without loosening selectivity.** Widen what you *observe* per round (more baskets evaluated, more venues, longer daily coverage), keeping the NEX-0057 acceptance bar fixed. This grows the denominator and the passes proportionally without changing what "pass" means.
- **Pre-register a looser rule as its own thing (call it NEX-0058):** fix its thresholds *before* seeing which baskets pass this window, then collect *its* 100 out-of-sample. Don't retrofit thresholds to the 4.75 days you already looked at.
- **Run a power calculation instead of assuming 100.** +4.07% vs +1.85% at 24h (35/58 up) may already be near significance at n=13–58 depending on dispersion; you may not need 100, or you may find you need far more than 100 once costs and variance are in. Decide the N from the effect size, not the calendar.

And note the cost drag your +% figures omit: live event-card fills carry a **0.2% taker fee per fill** (round-trip ≈ 0.4%), and the backtest stress estimate is 2% fee + 0.5% slippage per side. A +2.03% 6-hour gross edge is materially thinner after costs. Measured past edge is not a forecast — these trades can lose money.

## 2) A live card that carries a typical Hot crypto basket

**Yes — two live, tradeable-now crypto-basket cards exist** (confirmed via get_event_card_info this run; `status=live`, `trading_closes_at=null`, `tradeable_now=true`):

- **Closest match to a headline-derived Hot crypto basket:** card id **`ce0c9e32-84fa-44a2-93de-2da6651498a2`** — "Bitcoin and Ethereum surge past resistance as Solana DeFi volume hits all-time high…", ticker EVCDX-BITCOIN-AND-ETHEREUM-CE0C9E. Basket: **BTC / ETH / SOL / BCH** (4 members, so it clears a ≥3-member gate). Caveat for matching: it is **~96.8% BTC by weight** (ETH 2.6%, SOL 0.1%, BCH 0.4%), so its behaviour is nearly BTC itself — match it against your Hot basket's actual weights, not just its members.
- **More evenly-weighted multi-coin crypto card:** card id **`5d91bf43-a597-47b0-9abe-5c7f52618bbd`** — "AIB-Privacy — Privacy Crypto Index Basket". Basket: **ZEC ~70% / XMR ~30%** plus trace-weight privacy legs (PART, WAN, AZTEC, …).

Not usable right now: card `150abcfc-a563-46e7-8d10-affb68f40589` ("AIB-C-AI — Crypto AI Index Basket") is `status=live` but **paused** (`tradeable_now=false`, stale index), so don't route to it until its index refreshes.
